docs.title: REFA API
docs.text: Documentation for the REFA API: how to authenticate, how to query the endpoints, and the full description of the request payloads.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The REFA API calculates feasible transmission line upgrade projects (Rebuild, Reconductoring, Voltage Upgrade, HVDC) and their lifecycle costs, given the characteristics of a line project and a set of candidate conductors.

The main endpoint, /calculate-feasible-projects, is queried with the payload_calculate-feasible-projects.json file, whose structure and fields are described in Payload Structure.

The API accepts payloads in either metric or imperial units. See Unit Systems for details.

docs.title: Base URL
docs.text: https://refa-202610-lbl-d8-refa.pantheonsite.io

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text: Method Endpoint Description POST /refa-api/v1/calculate-feasible-projects Calculate feasible transmission line upgrade projects and their costs (main endpoint, see Payload Structure)

docs.title: Authentication (OAuth2 client credentials)
docs.text:
All requests must carry a bearer access token. Tokens are obtained from the OAuth token endpoint using HTTP Basic client authentication:

  • Token URL: https://refa-202610-lbl-d8-refa.pantheonsite.io/oauth/token
  • Client credentials (CLIENT_ID / CLIENT_SECRET): get them from the REFA API admin panel, under "API Keys".
  • Grant type: client_credentials
  • Scope: refa:calculate

Token request (the Authorization header is Basic base64(CLIENT_ID:CLIENT_SECRET)):

curl -X POST "https://refa-202610-lbl-d8-refa.pantheonsite.io/oauth/token" \
  -u "$CLIENT_ID:$CLIENT_SECRET" \
  -d "grant_type=client_credentials" \
  -d "scope=refa:calculate"

Response:

{
  "access_token": "eyJhbGciOi...",
  "token_type": "Bearer",
  "expires_in": 3600,
  "scope": "refa:calculate"
}

docs.title: Querying the calculate-feasible-projects endpoint
docs.text:
Send the payload as a JSON body with the bearer token:

curl -X POST "https://refa-202610-lbl-d8-refa.pantheonsite.io/refa-api/v1/calculate-feasible-projects" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @payload_calculate-feasible-projects.json

Equivalent Python for a ready-to-run script:

import base64, json
from urllib.parse import urlencode
from urllib.request import Request, urlopen

CLIENT_ID = "..."       # from the REFA API admin panel, under "API Keys"
CLIENT_SECRET = "..."   # from the REFA API admin panel, under "API Keys"
TOKEN_URL = "https://refa.lbl.gov/oauth/token"
API_URL = "https://refa.lbl.gov/refa-api/v1/calculate-feasible-projects"

# 1. Get the access token
credentials = base64.b64encode(f"{CLIENT_ID}:{CLIENT_SECRET}".encode()).decode("ascii")
token_request = Request(
    TOKEN_URL,
    data=urlencode({"grant_type": "client_credentials", "scope": "refa:calculate"}).encode(),
    headers={"Authorization": f"Basic {credentials}",
             "Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"},
    method="POST",
)
with urlopen(token_request, timeout=60) as response:
    access_token = json.load(response)["access_token"]

# 2. Send the payload
with open("payload_calculate-feasible-projects.json", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    payload = json.load(f)
api_request = Request(
    API_URL,
    data=json.dumps(payload).encode(),
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {access_token}",
             "Content-Type": "application/json"},
    method="POST",
)
with urlopen(api_request, timeout=120) as response:
    results = json.load(response)

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
1. Units Consistency: Ensure all units are consistent with the specifications above. Mixing units (e.g., miles and kilometers) will cause errors.

  2. Temperature Ranges: Conductor temperatures should follow: temp_dc_c ≤ temp_low_c ≤ temp_high_c ≤ max_temperature_c (or the _f equivalents in imperial payloads).

  3. Economic Parameters: The wacc and inflation values should be in decimal form (e.g., 7% = 0.07).

  4. Binary Flags: Fields like consider_losses, consider_corona, etc., use 0 for false and 1 for true.

docs.title: Payload Structure
docs.text:
This section explains the structure and fields of the payload_calculate-feasible-projects.json file, the request body of the /calculate-feasible-projects endpoint.

The payload JSON contains eight main sections:

  1. project_options - Configuration for different upgrade options (rebuild, reconductoring, e.g.)
  2. conductors - List of available conductor types and specifications
  3. existing - Current transmission line configuration (if known to the user)
  4. data - Project-level parameters
  5. line_design - Physical line design specifications
  6. environment - Installation environment and location parameters
  7. loading - Mechanical loading conditions
  8. economics - Economic analysis parameters

docs.title: project_options
docs.text: Defines different upgrade scenarios to evaluate. Each option represents a different approach to upgrading the transmission line.

docs.title: Available Options:
docs.text:
• Rebuild - Complete line rebuild
  • Reconductoring - Replace conductors only
  • Voltage Upgrade - Increase voltage level
  • HVDC - Convert to High Voltage Direct Current

docs.title: Fields for Each Option:
docs.text: Field Type Unit Description option string - Name of the upgrade option structure_remaining_life integer years Remaining useful life of structures (0 = replace) conductor_remaining_life integer years Remaining useful life of conductors (0 = replace) voltage_kv integer kV Operating voltage level structure_upgrade integer 0/1 Whether structures need upgrading (0=no, 1=yes) nbr_bundles integer - Number of conductor bundles per phase nbr_conds_per_bundle integer - Number of conductors per bundle cost_of_structures_dol_per_unit integer $/unit Cost per structure unit

docs.title: conductors
docs.text: Array of conductor specifications. Each conductor object contains detailed electrical, mechanical, and thermal properties.

docs.title: Conductor Types Available:
docs.text:
• ACSR - Aluminum Conductor Steel Reinforced
  • ACSS - Aluminum Conductor Steel Supported
  • ACCC - Aluminum Conductor Composite Core
  • AECC - Aluminum Ecapsulated Carbon Core
  • ACCR - Aluminum Conductor Composite Reinforced
  • ACCS - Aluminum Conductor Composite Supported

docs.title: Conductor Fields:
docs.text: Field Type Unit Description type string - Conductor type (ACSR, ACSS, ACCC, etc.) code string - Conductor code/name (e.g., "795.0_DRAKE") cost_dol_per_km number $/km Material cost per kilometer installation_cost_dol_per_km number $/km Installation cost per kilometer accessories_cost_dol_per_km number $/km Accessories cost per kilometer area_mm2 number mm² Cross-sectional area diameter_mm number mm Conductor diameter weight_n_per_m number N/m Weight per unit length conductor_rts_kn number kN Rated tensile strength temp_dc_c number °C DC resistance reference temperature temp_low_c number °C AC Low operating temperature temp_high_c number °C AC High operating temperature max_temperature_c number °C Maximum allowable temperature res_dc_ohm_per_m number Ω/m DC resistance at reference temperature res_low_ohm_per_m number Ω/m Resistance at AC low temperature res_high_ohm_per_m number Ω/m Resistance at AC high temperature elastic_modulus_gpa number GPa Elastic modulus (Young's modulus) coeff_thermal_expan_per_c number 1/°C Coefficient of thermal expansion emissivity number - Surface emissivity (0-1) solar_absorptivity number - Solar absorptivity (0-1) rugosity_coefficient number - Surface roughness coefficient

docs.title: existing
docs.text: Describes the current transmission line configuration before any upgrades.

docs.title: Fields:
docs.text:
Field Type Unit Description nbr_circuits integer - Number of circuits nbr_conds_per_bundle integer - Number of conductors per bundle type string - Current conductor type code string - Current conductor code

Plus all conductor specification fields (same as in conductors section) and structure specification fields (same as in Structures Sub-object).

docs.title: data
docs.text:
Project-level configuration and analysis parameters.

Field Type Unit Description prj_name string - Project name/identifier power_mw number MW Required/New power capacity voltage_kv number kV Operating voltage load_factor number - Load factor (0-1, typical 0.63) consider_losses integer 0/1 Include electrical losses in analysis (0=no, 1=yes) consider_corona integer 0/1 Include corona losses in analysis (0=no, 1=yes) consider_str_type integer 0/1 Consider structure type in analysis (0=no, 1=yes) customize_inv_options integer 0/1 Allow customized investment options (0=no, 1=yes) include_infeasible integer 0/1 Include infeasible conductors in results when their performance in terms of ampacity, sag, or corona is desired even if they don't satisfy the requirements (0=no, 1=yes)

docs.title: line_design
docs.text:
Physical design specifications of the transmission line.

Field Type Unit Description nbr_circuits integer - Number of circuits nbr_conds_per_bundle integer - Number of conductors per bundle length_km number km Total line length nbr_structures integer - Total number of structures max_span_m number meters Maximum span length avg_span_m number meters Average span length max_sag_m number meters Maximum conductor sag

docs.title: environment
docs.text:
Environmental and meteorological conditions for the line location.

Field Type Unit Description latitude number degrees Geographic latitude atmosphere string - Atmospheric condition (e.g., "Clear") elevation_m number meters Elevation above sea level date string YYYY-MM-DD Reference date day integer - Day of month month integer - Month (1-12) year integer - Year hour integer - Hour of day (0-23) wind_speed_m_per_s number m/s Wind speed wind_angle number degrees Wind direction angle cw_angle_direction_rel_to_north number degrees Conductor-wind angle relative to north ambient_temperature_c number °C Ambient air temperature temp_coeff_resistivity number 1/°C Temperature coefficient of resistivity weather_correction_factor number - Weather correction factor

docs.title: loading
docs.text:
Mechanical loading conditions and design criteria.

Field Type Unit Description initial_tension_percentage number - Initial tension as percentage of RTS (0-1) initial_temperature_c number °C Temperature at initial tension Loading string - Loading standard (e.g., "NESC_250B_Heavy") ice_density_kg_per_m3 number kg/m³ Ice density ice_thickness_m number meters Ice thickness on the conductor pressure_pa number Pa Wind pressure wind_speed_m_per_s number m/s Design wind speed wind_ice_temperature_c number °C Temperature during ice/wind loading additive_loading_n_per_m number N/m Additional loading per unit length ld_select string - Selected loading case

docs.title: Common Loading Standards:
docs.text:
• NESC_250B_Heavy - National Electric Safety Code (NESC), Heavy loading
  • NESC_250B_Medium - NESC Medium loading
  • NESC_250B_Light - NESC Light loading

docs.title: economics
docs.text:
Economic analysis parameters for lifecycle cost calculations.

Field Type Unit Description conductors_lifetime integer years Expected conductor lifetime structures_lifetime integer years Expected structure lifetime conductor_remaining_life integer years Remaining life of existing conductors structure_remaining_life integer years Remaining life of existing structures cost_of_structures_dol_per_unit number $/unit Cost per structure unit wacc number - Weighted Average Cost of Capital (decimal, e.g., 0.07 = 7%) inflation number - Annual inflation rate (decimal, e.g., 0.02 = 2%) cost_of_losses_dol_per_mwh number $/MWh Cost of electrical losses cost_of_congestion_dol_per_mwh number $/MWh Cost of transmission congestion cost_structures_modif_v_upgd_dol number $ Cost of structure modifications for voltage upgrade cost_structures_modif_hvdc_dol number $ Cost of structure modifications for HVDC conversion cost_substations_upgrade_dol number $ Substation upgrade costs cost_converters_dol number $ HVDC converter station costs

docs.title: Unit Systems
docs.text:
The API works internally with metric units, but clients may send requests in either unit system:

  • Metric payloads use metric field suffixes (e.g., distance_a_b_m, length_km, temp_high_c) — this is the format of payload_calculate-feasible-projects.json.
  • Imperial payloads use imperial field suffixes (e.g., distance_a_b_ft, length_mile, temp_high_f).

docs.title: How the API handles each unit system
docs.text:
Request What the API does Response Metric payload Uses the values as-is Metric field names and values, plus "unit_system": "metric" Imperial payload Converts all values to metric on entry, then runs the analysis Imperial field names and values (converted back from the metric results), plus "unit_system": "imperial"

Unit-system detection is automatic: the API inspects the field names (and the optional top-level "unit_system" field) of the payload, so no extra parameter is required.

Fields without a unit suffix (percentages, costs in $, kV, MW, degrees, dimensionless ratios, etc.) are identical in both unit systems and are left unchanged.

Technical-performance fields returned by the engine are also converted and renamed, e.g.:

  • sag_m → sag_ft, sag_at_loading_m → sag_at_loading_ft
  • max_sag_m → max_sag_ft
  • temp_at_ampacity_c → temp_at_ampacity_f
  • total_force_n → total_force_lbf, tension_n → tension_lbf

Dimensionless or non-length results (ampacity_a, peak_current_a, resistance_at_ampacity_ohm_per_m, losses_at_peak_mwh_per_m, congestion_mw, costs in $, etc.) keep the same field names and values in both modes.
